name: agent-wolf-web
description: Agent Wolf UI — hypothesis list/detail, scoreboard, Orange chat iframe. Own components; imports nothing from agent-orange. See design/2026-08-20-agent-wolf.md (agent-orange repo).
comment: @agentkit/chat-ui — 🔴 BUMP THE VERSION ON EVERY REPUBLISH. The dependency above points at a tarball committed under web/vendor/, built in the OTHER repo (agent-orange: `cd web && npm run build && npm pack`). Under yarn 1, REPLACING that file at the SAME version updates NOTHING, and this was executed rather than read (2026-08-24, yarn 1.22.22): a dirty `yarn install` reports "Already up-to-date"; `yarn cache clean @agentkit/chat-ui` followed by `yarn install --force` still installs the old files; and even `rm -rf node_modules && yarn install --frozen-lockfile` — CI's situation — serves the STALE CACHED COPY without error, because yarn's cache key is name-version-lockfilehash and none of those three changed. Wolf then builds against components that are not the ones in the file, with NOTHING failing and nothing to see. (R134 predicted `error Integrity check failed` here; the observed behaviour is quieter and therefore worse.) So a republish is: bump `version` in agent-orange/web/package.json, re-pack, copy the NEW filename into web/vendor/, delete the old one, and update BOTH the range above and the filename it names — they must always agree, which web/src/theme.test.ts asserts against the INSTALLED package's version. Do NOT switch to the directory form "file:../../web": yarn 1 raw-copies web/node_modules with it, giving the consumer a second React, and both `files` and `.npmignore` are ignored. Owner decision 2026-08-24: no registry, both repos in lockstep, revisit when a third application appears. See design/2026-08-20-agent-wolf.md, R134 and R125.
